title: 第一卷 第5章 去镇上卖货
slug: 一路逃荒一路富手握空间带飞全家
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

从沈家村到青川镇，十里路，走官道要一个多时辰。

她脚程快，抄了一段田埂小路，省了小半刻钟。

到镇上的时候，集市刚开。

青川镇不算大，一条主街贯穿南北，两边是铺面和摊位。

赶集日人多，卖菜的、卖布的、卖陶罐的挤在一起，吆喝声此起彼伏。

沈鹿溪没急着找地方摆摊，先沿着主街走了一趟，把两边的铺子扫了一遍。

药铺有两家，一家在街头，招牌写着“仁和堂”，门面大，看着气派。

另一家在街尾拐角，招牌旧了，写着“济民药铺”，门面小，掌柜是个四十来岁的瘦男人，正坐在柜台后面打算盘。

茶铺一家，在街中段，门口摆着几个茶缸，伙计正在往里添水。

酒楼两家，一家大的叫“福满楼”，一家小的没挂招牌，门口支了个灶台在炸油饼。

沈鹿溪把这些都记在心里，转身先去了街尾的济民药铺。

大铺子规矩多，价格压得狠，还爱挑毛病。

小铺子好说话，掌柜自己收货自己卖，利润薄，给的价反而公道些。

这些门道是前世逃难路上学来的。

那时候她帮人跑过腿，给药铺送过货，知道里头的弯弯绕。

推门进去，药铺里弥漫着一股草药味，柜台上摆着几排药屉子，标签写得密密麻麻。

掌柜抬头看了她一眼，目光在竹筐上停了一下：“小姑娘，买药？”

“不买药，卖药。”沈鹿溪把竹筐放在柜台上，把草药一把一把拿出来摆好，“掌柜的，您看看这几样。”

掌柜放下算盘，凑过来瞧了瞧。

先拿起金银花，翻了翻，放在鼻子底下闻了闻，点了点头，又拿起柴胡，捏了捏根茎，眉头微微挑了一下。

“这柴胡不错，根茎粗壮，晒得也干净。你自己采的？”

“山上采的，自己晒的。”

掌柜又看了看黄芩，放下来，手指在柜台上敲了两下：“金银花我收，八文钱一两。柴胡品相好，给你十二文一两。黄芩差一些，六文。”

沈鹿溪没立刻答应。

她在心里算了一下。

金银花她采了大约三两，柴胡有二两多，黄芩一两半。

按这个价算下来，总共不到七十文。

“掌柜的，柴胡的行情我打听过，镇上仁和堂收价是十五文一两。您这儿给十二文，是不是低了点？”

她没打听过。

前世的记忆里，柴胡在青川镇的收价一直在十三到十五文之间浮动，这个价她记得清楚。

content_en:
Page (1/3)

It is ten miles from Shenjia Village to Qingchuan Town, and it takes more than an hour to take the official road.

She was fast on her feet and took a section of the path between the fields, saving her half an hour.

When we arrived in town, the market had just opened.

Qingchuan Town is not that big, with a main street running from north to south, with shops and stalls on both sides.

There are many people on market day. Vegetable sellers, cloth sellers, and pottery pot sellers are crowded together, and shouts come and go.

Shen Luxi was not in a hurry to find a place to set up a stall. He first walked along the main street and scanned the shops on both sides.

There are two drugstores. One is on the street. The signboard reads "Renhetang". It has a large appearance and looks impressive.

The other one is at the end of the street and on the corner. It has an old sign and reads "Jimin Drug Store". It has a small storefront and the shopkeeper is a thin man in his forties, sitting behind the counter with an abacus.

There is a tea shop in the middle of the street. There are several tea jars at the door, and the waiters are filling them with water.

There are two restaurants, the big one is called "Fumanlou", and the smaller one has no signboard and has a stove set up at the door to fry pancakes.

Shen Luxi kept all this in mind, turned around and went to Jimin Pharmacy at the end of the street.

Big shops have many rules, very low prices, and they like to find faults.

The shop is easy to talk to. The shopkeeper collects the goods and sells them himself. The profit is thin, so the price given is more reasonable.

These skills were learned while escaping from previous lives.

At that time, she had run errands for people and delivered goods to the drug store, so she knew the twists and turns inside.

Pushing open the door and walking in, the drug store is filled with the smell of herbal medicine. There are several rows of medicine drawers on the counter with densely written labels.

The shopkeeper looked up at her and paused on the bamboo basket: "Little girl, are you buying medicine?"

"Don't buy medicine, sell medicine." Shen Luxi put the bamboo basket on the counter, took out the herbs one by one and arranged them, "Shopkeeper, take a look at these."

The shopkeeper put down his abacus and came over to take a look.

First he picked up the honeysuckle, turned it over, put it under his nose and smelled it, nodded, then picked up the bupleurum, pinched the rhizome, and raised his brows slightly.

"This Bupleurum is good. The rhizome is thick and clean in the sun. Did you pick it yourself?"

"I pick it from the mountains and dry it myself."

The shopkeeper looked at the Scutellaria baicalensis again, put it down, and tapped his fingers twice on the counter: "I'll take the honeysuckle, eight cents and one tael. The Bupleurum is of good quality, I'll give you twelve cents and one tael. The Scutellaria baicalensis is a little worse, six cents."

Shen Luxi did not agree immediately.

She did the math in her head.

She picked about three taels of honeysuckle, more than two taels of bupleurum, and one and a half scutellaria baicalensis.

At this price, the total is less than seventy cents.

"Shopkeeper, I've inquired about the market price of Bupleurum. Renhetang in town charges fifteen cents per tael. Is the twelve cents you're offering here a bit low?"

She didn't ask.

In the memory of her previous life, the price of Bupleurum in Qingchuan Town had always fluctuated between thirteen and fifteen cents. She remembered this price clearly.
